subject: Post-call: Reliability discovery & proposed fallback options for AuroraFin
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Ross <ethan.ross@aurorafin.com>
Cc: sergio_alvarez@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 3 May 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap — reliability constraints & success criteria

Thanks again for taking the time today, Ethan — appreciate the candid discussion. Below is a short recap of what we heard, what matters to AuroraFin, and proposed next steps so we can align internally and with the SRE/infra team.

1) Top pain points you described
- Recurring availability incidents over the last 12 months (noted two major outages affecting API paths).
- Fallback behavior today degrades output quality substantially (clients get different results when system falls back to a smaller model).
- Lack of predictable SLAs and limited visibility into token-level cost when autoscaler behaves unexpectedly.

2) Current stack (as we understand it)
- Ingress/api: AWS ALB -> EKS (k8s autoscaling)
- Model hosting: in-house endpoints backed by mixed GPU pool (on-demand + spot); some regional failovers to us-west-2 only
- Observability: Prometheus + internal dashboard; no per-route token cost attribution yet

3) Success criteria AuroraFin mentioned
- Availability target: >= 99.95% monthly for production inference (per-route SLA request).
- Latency: p95 < 180ms for standard generation requests; p99 budget for heavier workloads.
- Graceful degradation: if primary model/region is unavailable, fallback should preserve quality above baseline (not just smaller model that produces wrong semantics).
- Cost predictability: clear visibility into per-token and per-session cost to reason about carrier and product economics.

4) Incident history details you volunteered
- Two production incidents in Q1: one due to scale-up failure (approx 3 hours), one due to AZ networking flakiness (approx 90 minutes).
- During incidents, traffic was routed to fallback instances running quantized models with ~15% drop in downstream conversion metrics.

5) How Redwood could help (initial proposal)
- Dedicated pilot (2-week canary) using a small reserved pool + cross-region secondary pool for failover.
- Canary policy: route 5–10% traffic through the dedicated pool initially, measure latency/cost/quality delta.
- Fallback strategy: implement model-variant fallback with output-preserving techniques (prefix-KV cache + reranking) before degrading to smaller model.
- Observability: deliver per-route token breakdown and incident tracing so we can pinpoint autoscaler vs infra vs model issues.

6) Immediate asks / next steps
- AuroraFin: share the incident report from Q1 and a short architecture diagram (EKS config + regions).
- Redwood: produce a short technical note on proposed canary & fallback policy (we'll include an ops playbook and SLO examples).
- Schedule follow-up with SRE + Eng manager (45m) next week to align on pilot scope and SLA language.

Proposed time: Wed 2026-05-06 10:00am PT — please confirm or suggest an alternative.

I'll loop in Sergio (cc'd) to sketch an initial canary plan and ballpark pricing.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-call recap — reliability constraints & success criteria

Thanks Vanessa — this is exactly the level of detail we need. A couple of clarifications and an attachment to share from our side.

Clarifications:
- The two Q1 outages you noted are accurate. The longer incident was an autoscaler + IAM rotation issue; the AZ networking issue was downstream but exposed a single-region dependency in our control plane.
- Our fallback today uses a smaller 8B distilled model; quality drop was measurable in our fraud-detection prompt (false positives rose ~22%).
- We are comfortable with a 5–10% canary window but will want to see quality metrics (precision/recall for the fraud prompts) within 48 hours of any change.

Attached: Q1 incident report (redacted).

We can do Wed 2026-05-06 10:00am PT — confirmed on my end. Please include an ops-level engineer and someone from product to sign off on success metrics.

Ethan Ross
Head of Engineering | AuroraFin
ethan.ross@aurorafin.com | +1 (617) 555-0188

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Ethan Ross <ethan.ross@aurorafin.com>
Date: Mon, 4 May 2026 08:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — reliability constraints & success criteria

Thanks Vanessa / Ethan — looping in a quick operational proposal before the Wed sync. High level:

- Canary + failover mechanics
  * Start with a dedicated small GPU pool in us-west-2 (reserved capacity for pilot).
  * Route 5% of production traffic via Redwood Dedicated; collect token-level cost, latency, and model output diffs.
  * If Dedicated pool detects performance regression, automatic rollback to primary; if region/infra failure, failover to secondary region (us-east-1) with warmed KV caches.

- Model fallback strategy (to address the quality drop you saw)
  * Prefer model-variant fallback (same architecture, lower capacity quantized weights) combined with reranking instead of switching to a distilled model.
  * Implement output-preservation safeguards: prompt-aware reranking, baseline checks for fraud prompts, and an immediate mitigation route that sends suspect traffic to a human-review queue rather than a lower-quality model.

- SLO/SLA recommendations (for negotiation)
  * Target pilot SLO: 99.9% availability for pilot traffic; production target: 99.95% with defined SLA credits for rollouts.
  * Incident detection & notification: 5-minute detection aim with 15-minute on-call acknowledgement.

- Ballpark commercial note
  * Pilot (2 weeks) + reserved pool + ops support: estimate $10k–$18k depending on GPU sizing and cross-region egress. We'll produce a refined quote after we see the call profile.

I'll attach a short canary plan draft for your internal review. Happy to walk through technical tradeoffs during Wed's meeting.

Sergio Alvarez
